claim_1.claim: Microarray Assay analysis of whole blood from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group) at days 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0) showed that the number of responsive genes was the largest for the pneumococcal vaccine group and the smallest for the saline control group, with the majority of changes seen at day 1 and day 7 compared to baseline.

sources.quote: Of the 3,102 transcripts for which abundance was significantly altered in response to vaccines, 239 changed by more than 2-fold in at least one time point.

It is thus possible to visualize that the number of responsive genes was the largest for the pneumococcal vaccine group and the smallest for the saline control group. Among the different time points, the majority of the changes were seen at days 1 and 7.

claim_2.claim: Microarray Assay analysis of whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) collected from 1.5 to 48 hr after vaccination (day 0) showed that significant changes in the transcription of genes forming the IFN response module were observed as early as 15 hr following influenza vaccination and persisted to 48 hr postvaccination, and analysis of isolated leukocyte populations 24 hr after influenza vaccination showed differences in IFN-inducible transcripts in neutrophils and monocytes.

sources.quote: Significant changes in the transcription of genes forming IFN response module were observed as early as 15 hr following administration of the vaccine and persisted to 48 hr postvaccination.
The analysis revealed differences in the levels of expression for IFN-inducible transcripts in neutrophils and in monocytes following influenza vaccination

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of whole blood at days 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0) showed 11-fold and 47-fold increases in the absolute numbers of plasmablasts following influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, respectively, with peak levels of 8.5 cells/uL and 71.7 cells/uL and a much greater expansion after pneumococcal vaccine compared to influenza vaccine.

sources.quote: Plasmablasts were identified by polychromatic flow cytometry in whole blood samples as CD19+/lo CD20−CD27+CD38hi plasmablasts and plasma cells.
There, 11-fold and 47-fold increases in the absolute numbers of plasmablasts were observed following vaccination with influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, respectively.
The peak levels reached a mean of 8.5 cells/uL and 71.7 cells/uL in response to influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, respectively.

claim_4.claim: Hemagglutinin Inhibition analysis of human sera at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) versus baseline (day 0) showed that in the influenza vaccine group, B Brisbane showed the strongest positive correlation between day 7 module M4.11 and an increase in HAI titers (r = 0.77).

sources.quote: Some day 7 modules correlating to levels of antibodies were similar to those found in the pneumococcal vaccine group (M4.11 and M4.10) (Figure 7B) with B Brisbane showing the strongest positive correlation with M4.11 and an increase in HAI titers (r = 0.77).

claim_5.claim: Virus-neutralization assays analysis of human sera at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) versus baseline (day 0) showed that day 28 antibody titer fold change over baseline was correlated with day 7 baseline-normalized averaged modular expression profiles for influenza vaccine strains.

sources.quote: Correlations between day 7 baseline-normalized averaged modular expression profiles and fold change of day 28 antibody titer over baseline for all available pneumococcal serotypes and influenza vaccine strains are represented on a heatmap.
(B) shows influenza vaccine (D28/baseline fold change [FC] in virus neutralization [VN] and hemagglutinin [HAI] titers).

claim_6.claim: commercial immunoassays analysis of antibody response to 14 pneumococcal polysaccharides at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) versus baseline (day 0) showed that day 7 modular transcriptional data in the pneumococcal vaccine group had the strongest positive correlations for modules M3.3 and M4.11 and strong negative correlations for inflammation modules M3.2, M4.2, and M4.13.

sources.quote: The strongest correlations were observed between day 7 modular transcriptional data and serology results in the pneumococcal vaccine group. The strongest positive correlations were found for modules M3.3 (annotated as cell cycle) and M4.11 (plasma cells) and to a lesser extent M4.10 (B cells), M5.10 and M6.2 (both associated with mitochondrial respiration). Strong negative correlations were observed at the same time point for modules associated with inflammation (M3.2, M4.2, and M4.13).

claim_7.claim: Multiplex Cytokine Analysis analysis of sera on day 1 after influenza vaccination (day 1) showed that serum levels of the IFN-inducible chemokine CXCL10 (IP-10) increased significantly compared to baseline.

sources.quote: Furthermore, serum levels of the IFN-inducible chemokine CXCL10 (IP-10) were also found to increase significantly on day 1 after influenza vaccination (p < 0.01; Figure S4).
